title: Console GA surface trim & rollout gating (dashboards, tracing, cost)
creator: Lina Cho
description: We must reduce the initial Console surface for GA to a narrow, production-safe telemetry set focused on three feature pillars: lightweight dashboards, sampled tracing, and a top-level cost breakdown. This ticket defines the explicit cuts, acceptance criteria, and rollout gating so engineering, design, and SRE can implement a predictable, observable launch with clear fallbacks.
background: The broader Console vision includes many cards, deep per-route token breakdowns, and always-on 100% tracing ingestion. Given time and cost constraints, marketing and leadership agreed to ship a hardened, lower-cost GA experience that meets SLAs and is easy to support. This work unblocks Dedicated and Private customers who require a stable Console surface for initial adoption.
decisions: Limit dashboard to a single ‘Overview’ page containing 6 prioritized cards: Total Requests, Mean P95 Latency, Error Rate, Top 10 Models by Token Volume, Cost Snapshot (30d), and Route Health summary.
Defer token-level per-request cost explorer (will be in console-2025.07). Initial Cost Snapshot aggregates by route and model only.
Tracing ingestion will use default 1% sampling for GA; customers may opt-in to higher sampling via Dedicated/Enterprise feature flag. Cost of always-on tracing is delegated to later cycles.
Telemetry retention: Metrics 30 days, Traces sampled (1%) with latest 7-day hot window indexed; longer retention is an add-on.
Feature gating: use runtime feature flag 'console.ga_minimum_surface' for staged rollout and rollback.
Graceful degradation: if metrics backend lag > 60s or errors exceed threshold, show an ‘insights degraded’ state and provide a link to the fallback raw logs view.
All rundown decisions documented in Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood-inference.internal/console/ga-trim-decision-log
acceptance_criteria: Overview page renders within 800ms median on a standard 50ms backend latency synthetic test.
Dashboard cards display consistent data with backend queries under 5s for 95% of requests.
Tracing pipeline accepts and indexes sampled traces up to 10k spans/day without exceeding the cost guardrails defined in ENG-22110.
Cost Snapshot shows top-10 routes and top-5 models with cost estimates accurate within ±15% versus billing reconciliation job.
Feature flag 'console.ga_minimum_surface' allows 10% canary rollout -> 50% -> 100% with automatic rollback if SLO breach occurs.
Design sign-off on visual affordances for ‘degraded’ and ‘limited data’ states (DES-1023 approved).
E2E smoke tests exist covering rendering, sampling toggle behavior, and canary rollback path.
Runbook updated with playbook for degraded telemetry scenarios and cost spikes (ops-runbook link included).
rollout_plan: Week 0: Merge MVP UI + backend shims behind feature flag; internal alpha in staging.
Week 1: 10% canary in prod for non-sensitive orgs. Monitor latency, errors, ingestion rate for 72h.
Week 2: Expand to 50% if no regression; run billing reconciliation against cost snapshot.
Week 3: 100% rollout and GA announcement if all gates pass; escalate to emergency rollback if any gate fails.
Post-GA: Collect qualitative feedback, prioritize add-ons (token-level costs, longer trace retention) into backlog for console-2025.07 cycle.
